gloss_en: azut — boldness/brazenness (עַזּוּת), the abstract noun for audacity of spirit; in Likutey Moharan primarily holy boldness (azut di-kedushah, 'be bold as a leopard') required to enter holiness, approach the true shepherds/tzaddikim, and stand in prayer, attained through joy and linked to the 'voice of strength' (kol oz); with its counterfeit counterpart, the brazenness of the Sitra Achra ('kingship without a crown')
